opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
Today, reading Mark left me in a knot with questions. The Jewish leaders approach Jesus and ask Him by what authority He is doing these things. Instead of answering directly, Jesus responds with a question of His own: “Was John’s baptism of heavenly origin or human origin?” And this is where I got stuck.
What exactly is Jesus asking? Is He asking whether John himself was baptized by heavenly origin? Is He asking whether John baptizing Jesus was heavenly? Is He talking about John’s ministry itself? Somewhere else in the Gospels, John says that he baptizes with water, but Christ will baptize with fire. So what exactly is happening here?
Perhaps the question itself is larger than I first thought.
Jesus is not asking whether John personally received baptism from heaven. He is asking whether John’s authority, mission, and ministry came from God or simply from man. Did John invent this movement? Or was he truly sent?
And suddenly the leaders are trapped. Because if they answer, “From heaven,” then they must explain why they rejected John, ignored his call to repentance, and dismissed the very one John pointed toward. And if they answer, “From man,” they lose the crowd, because many believed John was a prophet. So they choose safety: “We do not know.”
But perhaps Jesus already answered their question without answering it directly. Because John’s entire mission pointed somewhere: toward Him.
John was baptized with water. Water prepared. Water called people to repentance. Water washed externally as a sign that something internally needed changing. But John himself says someone greater is coming: “I baptize with water… He will baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire.”
Fire transforms. Fire purifies. Fire changes what it touches.
John prepared people for God. Christ brings people into communion with God.
And perhaps this is why Mark keeps returning to the same themes repeatedly: authority, baptism, fruit, repentance, faith. The deeper question underneath all of them seems to be: Who truly speaks with the authority of God?
John points. Jesus fulfills. The leaders resist. And eventually the reader is left to decide.  But we already know how history unfolds. I am certain you will choose correctly.  But allow yourself time to acknowledge this meeting, Jesus walking through the temple, as the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders approach him.  Wow!!  Then Jesus says, “Answer me.”  I’ll leave it here.  God Blesses, and God listens.
